texts: MYTH: Coffee dehydrates you. TRUTH: While caffeine has mild diuretic properties, the water content in coffee more than compensates. Studies show regular coffee consumption actually contributes to your daily hydration—your morning cup is hydrating you, not drying you out.

MYTH: Coffee stunts your growth. TRUTH: This widespread myth originated from poorly designed 1970s studies and has been thoroughly debunked. Modern research shows no link between caffeine consumption and stunted growth in any age group—it's one of the most persistent false beliefs about coffee with zero scientific basis.

MYTH: You should wait to drink coffee until you feel tired. TRUTH: By the time you feel tired, adenosine (the sleep chemical) has already built up in your brain. Caffeine works best when consumed proactively—research shows the optimal window is between 9:30 AM and 11:30 AM when your body's natural cortisol levels are declining, making the caffeine more effective.
